evidence.why: All interpolated values including URL placeholders (resetUrl, supportUrl, preferencesUrl) placed inside href="{{...}}" are passed through generic HTML escaping only, not escapeUrl; escapeHtml does not block javascript:/data: protocols, so a value like 'javascript:alert(1)' passes through unescaped in substance and becomes an executable href on click.

A protocol-allowlisting escapeUrl function exists in the codebase but is never called from notification-template.ts; the href attribute interpolation uses escapeHtml instead, so the protective control is present but not wired to the surface it protects.
additionalVars accepts arbitrary string values for any allowlisted key (including resetUrl/supportUrl/preferencesUrl) from the API request body, making the href value attacker-controlled.

controls_present: escapeUrl helper (unused at the vulnerable surface)
other_classes_observed: blocklist-based sanitisation (validateCustomTemplate) instead of allowlist/true sanitiser, which is bypassable
